legend.target_workload: the workload nominated before timing; its whole-model win must repeat before installation
legend.timing_case: the captured input case behind this hypothesis's local kernel timings
legend.timing_workload: the workload behind a region's recorded shipped-kernel speedup
legend.model_ratios: per-workload products of incremental model ratios; diagnostic estimates, not final measurements
legend.p: share of one step this region costs, all copies together, per workload
legend.T_orig_ms: library time for all copies, per workload, from pricing
legend.T_rep_ms: library time for one copy, per workload, from pricing
legend.roofline_ms: estimated ideal cost of one copy from boundary traffic and arithmetic
legend.s_max: optimistic headroom estimate: library time divided by estimated ideal cost
legend.bound: estimated limiting resource: memory, known compute, or launch; custom arithmetic may be unknown
legend.s: speedup shipped: the library's time over the shipped kernel's, both from the kernel's own ship clock
legend.region_ms: the kernel's time for one pass of one copy, from the ship clock
legend.library_ms: the library's time for the same pass, measured beside it
legend.win_ms: library_ms minus region_ms; positive means the kernel is faster
legend.sigma_ms: uncertainty of win_ms; a ship needs a win past three of these
legend.stranded: regions dropped before the search, grouped by reason
legend.steps_per_sample: dependent model steps in one timed sample of the step clock; more than one when a step is too short to bring the GPU clock up on its own
legend.min_win_ms: the least a region win had to save per step on this workload: 1% of the step, at most constants.min_win_ms; the three-sigma rule decides the rest
legend.speedup_vs_plain: under the compiled baseline: the finished model against plain eager MLX, paired in one window at the end of the job; compile's own gain is included, since the model runs compiled
legend.speedup_vs_compiled: under the plain baseline: the finished model (eager plus its kernels) against the untouched model under mx.compile, measured the same way; under 1 means compile alone is faster
legend.plain_win_confirmed: whether that comparison resolved a win past three sigma (compiled_win_confirmed likewise)
legend.plain_loss_confirmed: whether it resolved a loss (compiled_loss_confirmed likewise)
legend.measured_compute_gflops: the plain-matmul rate per dtype clocked in the region's own pricing window; the compute term of its estimated limit divides the region's flops by it
legend.close_rule: why a region's search ended: its budget or the job's is spent, the operator asked to finish, or no discernible headroom (launch-bound, head unmoved by the last two attempts, the last three kernels each within one sigma of the launch floor clocked beside them)
legend.constants.openers_per_region: how many attempts a region's widening round holds at most, each an opener written against the scaffold from a different agent-generated direction; limited by the remaining attempt budget
legend.delivery: how a kernel installs at the region's scope, per workload: direct, graph (the scope compiled with the cut inserted) or replay
legend.library_arm: what the region's clocks ran the library as, per workload: plain ops, or one compiled graph where graph delivery compiles the scope
legend.baseline.clocks_ms.compiled: under library inference: the model with its outermost compilable scopes compiled and empty, the baseline unless the manifest asks for plain
legend.final.delivery: under a plain baseline: the untouched model against the installed scopes compiled with no kernel, and that against the patched model

hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: Collapse both ops into one register pass: each thread reads in0[i] and in1[i], computes in1 + precise::tanh(in0) and writes out0[i]. Removes the scratch buffer round trip and the device barrier, and launches 4096 threads in 256-wide groups so 16 threadgroups spread over the 10 cores instead of one group doing 32 serial iterations. Expected to cut most of the 13 us scaffold time; the math stays identical so bits match.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: Same fused math but each thread handles four contiguous elements via float4 loads/stores (1024 threads, groups of 128). Differs from fused_elem by trading thread count for wider memory transactions; tests whether fewer, wider threads win at this tiny size where launch/scheduling overhead dominates.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: Keep the scaffold's single 128-thread threadgroup and grid-stride loop but fuse the two ops so no scratch/barrier is needed. Isolates how much of the scaffold's cost is the scratch round trip versus the lack of multi-core spread, compared with fused_elem.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: Launch exactly one 256-thread threadgroup per GPU core (10 groups, 2560 threads), each thread grid-striding over elements. Differs from fused_elem (16 small groups, one element each) and fused_single_tg (one group) by matching group count to cores while keeping per-thread loop work, testing whether occupancy-matched striding beats one-element-per-thread.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: All fused variants sit at about 4.85 us, roughly 1 us above the floor probe, so per-dispatch argument setup is the remaining lever. This kernel never names in0_shape, so the harness binds only in0, in1, out0 (no shape buffer encode); n is fixed at 4096 with a fallback_predicate guarding other sizes. Tests whether trimming bound arguments shaves dispatch overhead.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: 4096 threads in 32-thread groups (128 groups) so the scheduler can fill every core with many tiny groups at once; tests whether group granularity rather than group count reduces the tail of the dispatch.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: 512 threads in 64-thread groups (8 groups), each thread computing eight strided elements scalar; tests whether a much smaller thread launch has lower fixed cost than 4096 or 2560 threads while still using multiple cores.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: Every fused variant clusters at 4.5 us regardless of thread layout, so the remaining fixed cost may be in how the harness binds the kernel: this body omits the T template and shape buffers entirely, using float directly, 2048 threads each handling two adjacent elements, to test whether a non-templated, minimal-argument pipeline shaves dispatch overhead.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: Launch as a 64x64 2D grid with 8x8 threadgroups (64 groups of 64); tests whether a 2D dispatch shape maps onto cores differently from the 1D grids tried so far, all of which sat at 4.5 us.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: One maximal 1024-thread threadgroup where each thread processes four contiguous elements via float4; fused_single_tg with 128 threads was 11.7 us because it serialized on one core, but a 1024-wide group uses the core's full SIMD width and avoids any multi-group scheduling; tests whether a single fat group is cheaper to launch than many groups.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: one thread per element across cores
hypotheses.hypothesis: the scaffold serializes 4096 elements through one 128-thread group on a single core; launching 4096 threads in 32 groups of 128 spreads the adds across all 10 cores, cutting the per-group serial loop to one element and removing the loop overhead. Expected: drop from 6.5 us toward the 3.5 to 4.5 us fixed dispatch floor seen in the previous region.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: 1024 threads each load one float4 from in0 and in1 and store one float4, reinterpreting the device pointers; fewer, wider memory transactions and fewer active threads per core. Differs from elem_spread by trading thread count for transaction width; tests whether wider loads matter at this size.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: 128 groups of 32 threads (one simdgroup each), one element per thread: minimum-latency groups that the scheduler can place across cores quickly, testing whether small-group dispatch granularity lowers fixed cost versus 128-thread groups.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: two elements per thread without template or shape buffers
hypotheses.hypothesis: 2048 threads each handle two consecutive elements with hard-coded 4096 and no T template or shape buffers bound, minimizing argument binding and halving thread count; differs from the others by removing all harness-passed metadata while keeping the grid wide.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: 1024 float4 threads in four 256-thread groups instead of eight 128-thread groups: fewer threadgroup dispatches for the same per-thread work; tests whether group count, not thread count, is the residual cost above the library.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: float4 strided loop, half the threads
hypotheses.hypothesis: 512 threads each process two float4 pairs with a grid-stride loop (index i and i+512), halving thread count while keeping wide transactions; tests whether a smaller grid with independent loads in flight lowers dispatch time for a pure add.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: 1024 float4 threads in sixteen 64-thread groups (two simdgroups each): more, smaller groups than vec4_load to spread across all 10 cores with wide loads; combines the tg32 and vec4 ideas which each measured at the floor separately.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: 1024 float4 threads in a single 1024-thread group: the minimum number of threadgroups (one) for wide loads. vec4_big_groups (4 groups of 256) was the best measured at 4.12 us and trended better with fewer groups; this tests whether the fixed cost drops further at the one-group extreme, accepting single-core bandwidth since 48 KB is tiny.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: 4096 scalar threads in four 1024-thread groups, no bounds check: same group count as vec4_big_groups but scalar accesses and maximal occupancy per group; tests whether wide loads or group count drove the 4.12 us result.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: repeat the best layout (four 256-thread float4 groups) with the bounds branch removed and a single fused expression, removing the only conditional; tests whether the 4.12 us was real and whether branch removal helps at the margin.

hypotheses.hypothesis: every layout tried sits ~1.7-2 us above the library, so layout is not the lever; the library's own tanh kernel likely calls metal::tanh rather than metal::precise::tanh. With fast-math pinned by the harness the plain overload may compile to a shorter instruction sequence while remaining bit-identical under the exact rule; if the bits differ the harness rejects it and we learn the library's function choice.
